claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1).
claims.reason: The reply states the refund amount actually handled as 49.00 yuan (4900 cents). Per the customer's correction, the target invoice is INV-2026-0101 (two settled 4900 payments PAY-88100/PAY-88101, due 4900), so the overcharge is exactly 4900 cents with no remainder. The execution ledger confirms a completed refund of amount_cents 4900 on PAY-88101 (/view/execution), matching the requested complete outcome rather than a smaller amount, so there is no unstated remainder.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1).
claims.reason: The corrected target is INV-2026-0101 (the customer withdrew INV-2026-0142). Its second settled full payment PAY-88101 (4900 cents) is the refundable duplicate. The execution ledger and workflow events show refund RF-00001-056aa1 for PAY-88101 with status "completed", send_result 201 succeeded, and verification "matched_success" — i.e. accounting completion based on a verified receipt. The reply accurately states the 49.00 yuan refund on PAY-88101 was issued and gives the refund id, matching the observed execution result rather than substituting a policy answer.

claims.quote: refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1)
claims.reason: The customer's follow-up correction (/public_dialogue/2) re-scoped the case to INV-2026-0101 and said the original invoice should not be refunded. The final reply describes only a refund on PAY-88101, which per /view/evidence/3 belongs to INV-2026-0101 (September 2026), and the execution ledger confirms the completed refund RF-00001-056aa1 on PAY-88101. It makes no reference to the superseded October proposal (INV-2026-0142 / PAY-88213), so the reply matches the actually submitted correction.

rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. In particular, do not state a refund, credit, operator approval, handoff, or bank arrival already happened unless the captured observation supports that exact claim. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.
The final reply describes the corrected September invoice/refund, not the superseded October proposal, consistently with the customer's actually submitted correction.
